bib.title: Blending Is All You Need: Cheaper, Better Alternative to Trillion-Parameters LLM

question: Can a group of moderately sized chat LLMs, combined by randomly choosing which one writes each reply, match or beat a single much larger chat LLM on user retention and engagement?
hypothesis: A blend of small chat AIs gives more engaging and diverse conversations than any component, and can match or beat a 175B+ model at the inference cost of one small model.
contributions: Blended: per-turn uniform random selection of the responding chat AI from a set, so later turns condition on earlier turns written by other models
Large-scale A/B tests on the Chai platform comparing Blended (three 6-13B models) to GPT-3.5 (175B) and to its components
Retention and engagement summary statistics from log-log fits (delta-zeta, delta-beta, delta-alpha, delta-gamma)

method.summary: Three fine-tuned open chat models (Pygmalion 6B, Chai Model 6B, Vicuna 13B) and OpenAI Davinci (GPT-3.5, 175B) were each served to separate groups of new Chai users in A/B tests over 30 days. Blended picks one of the three components uniformly at random for every response in a conversation. Retention and engagement are reported relative to Pygmalion 6B as control.
method.task: open-domain entertainment chat, evaluated by user retention and engagement in live A/B tests

datasets.name: Chai Research platform live users
datasets.size: at least 10000 users in each group (text); 5,000 unique new users per model (Fig 1 caption)
datasets.split: independent randomly selected groups of new users, each served one chat AI

models.name: Pygmalion 6B
models.init_from: PygmalionAI/pygmalion-6b, further finetuned on conversational data with rejection sampling from a trained reward model

models.name: Chai Model 6B (ChaiLLM)
models.init_from: ChaiML/edit_sft_pyg_v2e_cp_17515, further finetuned on conversational data with rejection sampling from a reward model

models.name: Vicuna 13B (Vicuna+)
models.init_from: lmsys/vicuna-13b-v1.3, further finetuned on conversational data with rejection sampling from a reward model

models.name: Blended (13,6,6B)
models.architecture: ensemble; one component chosen uniformly at random per response

other.inference_cost: each response from a single component, so cost equals one 6B/13B system

inference.decoding: inferred: each component samples its reply; components use rejection sampling from a reward model (Irvine et al., 2023); no further detail
inference.samples: one A/B deployment per model; Blended draws theta_n uniformly (1/N, N=3) at every turn; no repeats or seeds stated

metrics.name: k-day user retention R(k) and test-to-control ratio q_n(k)
metrics.definition: R(k)=S_n(k)/|G_n|, fraction of the cohort active on day k; q_n(k)=R_n(k)/R_c(k)
metrics.unit: ratio; Fig 1 shows % improvement over control

metrics.name: user engagement E_n(t) and ratio r_n(t)
metrics.definition: fraction of cohort interacting in window t-delta to t+delta; proxy for average time spent per visiting user; r_n(t)=E_n(t)/E_c(t)
metrics.unit: ratio; Fig 1 shows % improvement over control

metrics.name: delta-zeta, delta-beta (retention) and delta-alpha, delta-gamma (engagement)
metrics.definition: intercept and slope of log-log best-fit lines of test-to-control ratio against day, with R*(k)=R(1)k^-beta and E*(t)=alpha t^gamma

metrics.name: Inference cost (FLOP)
metrics.definition: total floating point operations at test time divided by control (Pygmalion)

eval.protocol: independent A/B groups of real new users over 30 days; compared only through ratios to the control to cancel platform popularity and holiday effects; no significance test, confidence intervals or repeats reported

evidence.quote: Each model is assigned to 5,000 unique new users, graphs report the day 30 retention and engagement improvement with respect to the baseline.
We conduct a large-scale evaluation with at least 10000 users in each group, and we monitor the user engagement on the platform over a 30-day period.

limits: No confidence intervals, significance tests, repeats or seeds; each model is one deployment.
Group size is inconsistent: 'at least 10000 users in each group' in Sec 5.1 but 5,000 unique new users per model in the Fig 1 caption.
Day is inconsistent: Fig 1 caption says day 30; Sec 5.2 says the k=20 ratio.
Headline comparison appears only in Figs 1-3; bar values are not in the text, so only Table 1 fit parameters are citable numbers.
Table 1 has delta-zeta 0.0 for GPT-3.5 and no raw retention percentages are given; ratios are relative to Pygmalion 6B, and absolute retention or time spent are never reported.

Single platform (Chai, entertainment character chat) with its own audience; components were tuned on that platform's data and reward model, so the comparison with off-the-shelf GPT-3.5 is not like for like (no stated prompt or finetune for GPT-3.5).
GPT-3.5 is called 'Davinci (ChatGPT)'; model version, prompt and decoding for it are not given.
Cost shown as FLOPs only; no latency, memory, dollar cost, or serving setup is reported. Blending requires hosting all three models.
No ablation over number of components, selection distribution, or component pairs; uniform selection and larger selection sets are left as future work (Sec 6).
Mechanism ('best of all' characteristics through conditioning on history) is asserted, not tested.

terms.definition: randomly (and uniformly) selects the chat AI that generates the current response each turn
